task.notes: F, I and M all total 9.25. F leads on visual hierarchy, the most heavily weighted criterion, as the most convincing dense control room. I and M are a little more accessible (no contrast failures) and M has the best mobile layout, but M's empty right column at load and missing h1 put I ahead of it. L (9.0) is very close and arguably the most literal reading of the brief. H and E both have strong desktops but broken 390 px incident layouts (H truncated titles; E overlapping cells), so they score 8.0; H ranks above E for its zero contrast failures. G and N tie at 8.25: both are polished and accessible but ignore the density brief. B is the only submission missing RESPONSE.md, and its mobile view opens with the detail drawer covering the page. All 14 pages log a favicon 404 when served over http, which I ignore. I verified flows with Playwright at 1440 and 390 px (search empty state, severity filter, row select by mouse and keyboard, acknowledge), plus computed-style, contrast and geometry probes. I did not test with a real screen reader. The contrast scan is heuristic: it uses the nearest opaque ancestor background and skips SVG text.
